questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Winding road.
No parking.
Right lane closed.
Multiple turns.

questions.correctAnswerText: Winding road.
questions.explanation: This is a warning sign. Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign tells you the road ahead has curves and you should slow down.

questions.question: Guide signs are ____ signs that provide directional and mileage information to drivers.

options.text: Yellow
Red
Green
White

questions.correctAnswerText: Green
questions.explanation: Guide signs have a green background. They show directions and distances to specific places. They help you when driving in unfamiliar areas.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Entrance to full parking lots.
Entrance to road construction areas.
Entrance to dead-end streets.
Entrances from the wrong direction on one-way streets and expressway ramps.

questions.correctAnswerText: Entrances from the wrong direction on one-way streets and expressway ramps.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the road is one-way. You cannot enter from your current direction.

questions.question: A vehicle suddenly cuts in front of you, creating a hazard. What should you do first?

options.text: Honk and step on the brake firmly.
Take your foot off the gas pedal.
Swerve into the lane next to you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take your foot off the gas pedal.
questions.explanation: If a vehicle cuts in front of you, take your foot off the gas pedal. This creates space without making you slam on the brakes or swerve.

questions.question: Which of the following is most likely to be slippery in cold weather after snow or rain?

options.text: A hilly, open road
A residential road
A road in a shaded area

questions.correctAnswerText: A road in a shaded area
questions.explanation: Shaded areas freeze first and thaw last. On cold, wet days, these spots become icy before other parts of the road.

questions.question: Your vehicle strikes an unattended parked vehicle and you cannot locate the vehicle's owner. You:

options.text: Have done as much as you can.
Must stay until the police arrive.
Must leave a written notice containing your name, your address, and the circumstances of the accident.
May go on your way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must leave a written notice containing your name, your address, and the circumstances of the accident.
questions.explanation: If you hit a parked car and cannot find the owner, leave a written note with your name, address, and details about what happened.

questions.question: If you parallel park facing downward on a hill:

options.text: Turn your wheels sharply toward the side of the road.
Turn your wheels away from the side of the road.
Keep your wheels straight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your wheels sharply toward the side of the road.
questions.explanation: When parking downhill, turn your front wheels toward the curb. This stops your car from rolling into traffic if the brakes fail.

questions.question: If the driver of an oncoming vehicle fails to dim their headlights:

options.text: Look toward the center of the roadway.
Look toward the right side of the road.
Look straight ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look toward the right side of the road.
questions.explanation: Look toward the right side of the road to avoid being blinded by the bright headlights. This keeps you safe and lets you stay on your side of the road.

questions.question: A yellow light that flashes on and off means:

options.text: Stop and look for other vehicles, then go if there is no traffic.
Stop and wait for a green light.
Speed up to clear the intersection quickly.
Slow down and proceed with caution.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and proceed with caution.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means slow down and drive carefully through the intersection.

questions.question: You must not drive your vehicle at a speed greater than:

options.text: The maximum speed limit.
A speed that is faster than is reasonable and prudent.
A speed that is safe for existing conditions.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: You must obey the speed limit. You must also drive at a speed that is safe for the road, traffic, weather, and light conditions. You must drive at a reasonable speed for the area.

questions.question: You see a flashing red light at an intersection. What must you do?

options.text: Slow down and drive carefully through the intersection.
Turn right or left because the road ahead is blocked.
Stop and wait for a flashing green light.
Stop, then proceed when it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop, then proceed when it is safe.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means you must stop completely. Then you can go when the way is clear.

questions.question: You are stopped in the intersection waiting to turn left. What should you do?

options.text: Signal and turn your wheels to the left.
Signal and keep your wheels straight.
Flash your headlights so other drivers will let you through.
Drive around a car that blocks you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal and keep your wheels straight.
questions.explanation: Always signal before turning. Keep your wheels straight while waiting to turn left. If another car hits you from behind, straight wheels prevent you from being pushed into oncoming traffic.

questions.question: Your view to the side is blocked at an intersection. What should you do?

options.text: Slow down and look both ways.
Keep your speed and look both ways.
Stop, then move forward slowly until you can see both directions clearly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop, then move forward slowly until you can see both directions clearly.
questions.explanation: Stop at the intersection. Then move forward slowly until you can see clearly in both directions.

questions.question: You are in the left lane and want to move to the right lane. What should you do?

options.text: Check mirrors, signal, and look over your left shoulder before changing lanes.
Check mirrors, signal, and look over your right shoulder before changing lanes.
Check mirrors, signal, and look over both shoulders before changing lanes.
Check mirrors, signal, and change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check mirrors, signal, and look over your right shoulder before changing lanes.
questions.explanation: Look over your shoulder in the direction you want to move to check your blind spot. Always check your mirrors and use your signal before changing lanes.

questions.question: The light is green and you want to turn left, but traffic is coming. What should you do?

options.text: Use the next intersection instead.
Wait at the crosswalk for traffic to clear.
Wait in the middle of the intersection for traffic to clear.
Go because you have a green light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait in the middle of the intersection for traffic to clear.
questions.explanation: You can enter the intersection when the light is green. Wait in the center for oncoming traffic to pass before you turn left.

questions.question: What is a speed limit?

options.text: The fastest or slowest legal speed you can drive when conditions are dangerous.
The fastest or slowest legal speed you can drive when conditions are good.
The suggested speed to drive when conditions are good.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: The fastest or slowest legal speed you can drive when conditions are good.
questions.explanation: A speed limit is the fastest or slowest legal speed you can drive when conditions are good. You can drive slower, but never faster. Drive slower in school zones, work zones, and bad weather.

questions.question: An oncoming car has its bright headlights on and is blinding you. What should you do?

options.text: Use your bright lights until the other driver dims theirs.
Flash your lights to warn the other driver.
Dim your lights and speed up to pass quickly.
Look toward the right side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look toward the right side of the road.
questions.explanation: Look away from the bright headlights and toward the right side of the road. This keeps you from being blinded while the car passes.

questions.question: You stop at a stop sign. What should you do next?

options.text: Check your rearview mirror for cars behind you.
Move when the car ahead moves.
Look right, then left, then right again.
Look left, then right, then left again.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look left, then right, then left again.
questions.explanation: Look left first because traffic from the left is closer to you. Then look right. Then look left again to catch any traffic you might have missed.

questions.question: Does drinking coffee after drinking alcohol reduce alcohol in your body?

options.text: Yes, it lowers your blood alcohol level.
Yes, it cancels out the alcohol.
No, it has no effect on blood alcohol level.
No, it raises your blood alcohol level.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, it has no effect on blood alcohol level.
questions.explanation: Coffee cannot lower your blood alcohol level. It may keep you awake, but it does not change how much alcohol is in your body.

questions.question: How should you place your hands on the steering wheel to turn quickly?

options.text: On opposite sides of the steering wheel.
Next to each other at the top of the steering wheel.
One at the top and one at the bottom of the steering wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: On opposite sides of the steering wheel.
questions.explanation: Place both hands on opposite sides of the steering wheel. This position is comfortable and helps you turn safely on fast roads.

questions.question: Why is it important to watch for motorcycles?

options.text: They are harder to see than cars.
They rarely use their headlights.
Motorcycle riders are less skilled than other drivers.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: They are harder to see than cars.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles are small and easy to miss. They can hide in your blind spot. It is hard to judge how far away they are or how fast they are going. Always be alert and careful around motorcycles.

questions.question: Is it illegal for a car to share a lane with a motorcycle?

options.text: TRUE
FALSE

questions.correctAnswerText: TRUE
questions.explanation: Motorcycle riders have the right to use a full lane. Two motorcycles can share a lane, but a car cannot share a lane with a motorcycle.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Flagger ahead.
Turn left at the intersection.
Last turn before a toll road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Flagger ahead.
questions.explanation: Orange signs mean there is work zone activity. Watch for orange signs, cones, or barrels. Stay alert and expect changing road conditions. This sign tells you a flagger is coming. Follow the flagger's directions.

questions.question: You see a steady yellow light at an intersection ahead. You have not entered the intersection yet. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up to beat the red light.
Slow down and proceed carefully through the intersection.
Come to a safe stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a safe stop.
questions.explanation: A steady yellow light means prepare to stop. If you are already in the intersection, clear it safely. If you have not entered, stop.

questions.question: What should you do to help prevent crashes?

options.text: Communicate with other road users.
Ignore other drivers on the road.
Drive only on side streets and back roads.
Avoid driving during rush hour.

questions.correctAnswerText: Communicate with other road users.
questions.explanation: Crashes happen when drivers do something others don't expect. Let other drivers, cyclists, and pedestrians know what you are doing. Use your turn signal, brake lights, and horn when needed.

questions.question: At intersections, crosswalks, and railroad crossings, you should always:

options.text: Stop, listen, and proceed cautiously.
Look to the sides of your vehicle to see what is coming.
Slowly pass vehicles that seem to be stopped for no reason.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look to the sides of your vehicle to see what is coming.
questions.explanation: At places where people may cross or traffic lines meet, look left and right. Make sure no one is coming before you proceed.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Do not enter.
Roundabout ahead.
No U-turns.

questions.correctAnswerText: No U-turns.
questions.explanation: This is a regulatory sign. It tells drivers that U-turns are not allowed here.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Slow down or stop.
Stop, if necessary.
You must come to a complete stop.
Drive with caution and be ready to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: An eight-sided sign always means stop. You must come to a complete stop. Wait for all vehicles and pedestrians to pass before you go.

questions.question: When driving in bad weather, what should drivers do?

options.text: Speed up to reach their destination more quickly.
Follow the car ahead more closely.
Stay farther behind other vehicles.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay farther behind other vehicles.
questions.explanation: On wet roads, increase the distance between your vehicle and the car ahead. This gives you more time to stop safely.

questions.question: What can you do on a road with a broken white centerline?

options.text: You must stay in your lane.
You may cross the centerline to change lanes.
You may change lanes only from the left lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may cross the centerline to change lanes.
questions.explanation: White lines mean both lanes go the same direction. A broken white line means you may pass and change lanes when it is safe.
